headline: Athens Transforms Old Airport Into Europe's Second-Largest Park
meta_description: A former Athens airport is becoming Ellinikon Park, a 400-acre green refuge designed to cool the continent's hottest city by up to 7.2°F.
summary_short: Athens is converting its old airport into one of Europe's largest parks, with 30,000 trees and smart cooling systems to combat extreme heat.
body:
Athens is breathing new life into an abandoned airport site by building Ellinikon Park, a sprawling 400-acre urban forest that will become Europe's second-largest city park. Designed with scientific precision to combat the brutal Mediterranean heat, the project represents far more than just a recreational space—it's a climate adaptation strategy for a city that has long suffered under some of Europe's most punishing temperatures. Every element, from the placement of 30,000 trees to the positioning of 3 million smaller plants, has been engineered to keep the park 7.2°F cooler than surrounding pavement and concrete. Water features including misting systems and rainwater catchment basins will maintain moisture in the air, while shaded rest areas covering more than 60% of certain zones will offer genuine relief to residents.

The urgency behind this project reflects Athens's dire need for green space. The city once held the World Meteorological Organization record for Europe's highest temperature at 48.0°C (118.4°F), and it became the first European city to appoint a chief heat officer to manage heat wave crises. With a population double that of the nine next-largest Greek cities combined, Athens has long lacked adequate vegetation and open space. Recent efforts—including a micro-forest planted in 2024 under Mayor Haris Doukas and greening projects totaling 5,000 trees across neighborhoods—show momentum, but Ellinikon represents a transformative leap.

Designers maximized sustainability by repurposing hundreds of tons of concrete and rubble from the demolished airport infrastructure. The park will feature 520 plant species, with approximately three-quarters being native or well-adapted to local conditions. Smart irrigation systems and onsite water treatment will use non-potable water and harvested rainwater, ensuring the forest thrives despite low rainfall. The public is expected to access this green refuge starting next year.
quick_facts: 400-acre park in southern Athens, Europe's second-largest city park
30,000 trees and 3 million plants to keep air 7.2°F cooler
Athens holds Europe's heat record at 48.0°C (118.4°F)
Designed with smart irrigation and rainwater catchment systems
Opens to public in 2025, with further renovations planned for 2030
